name: IBM Code Modernization Rules
description: Comprehensive rules for modernizing legacy code to IBM standards

rules.description: Replace 'var' with 'const' or 'let'
rules.rationale: const and let provide block scoping and prevent hoisting issues

rules.description: Use arrow functions for callbacks and short functions
rules.rationale: Arrow functions provide cleaner syntax and lexical this binding

rules.description: Use template literals instead of string concatenation
rules.rationale: Template literals are more readable and less error-prone

rules.description: Use destructuring for object and array access
rules.rationale: Destructuring reduces code verbosity and improves readability

rules.description: Convert callback-based async to Promises
rules.rationale: Promises provide better error handling and avoid callback hell

rules.description: Use async/await instead of promise chains
rules.rationale: async/await provides cleaner, more readable asynchronous code

rules.description: Add try-catch blocks for async operations
rules.rationale: Proper error handling prevents unhandled promise rejections

rules.description: Replace require() with ES6 import statements
rules.rationale: ES6 modules are the standard and provide better tree-shaking

rules.description: Replace module.exports with ES6 export statements
rules.rationale: ES6 exports are more explicit and support named exports

rules.description: Remove hardcoded credentials and use environment variables
rules.rationale: Hardcoded credentials pose serious security risks

rules.description: Use prepared statements to prevent SQL injection
rules.rationale: Prepared statements prevent SQL injection attacks

rules.description: Add input validation for all user inputs
rules.rationale: Input validation prevents injection attacks and data corruption

rules.description: Add security headers using helmet
rules.rationale: Security headers protect against common web vulnerabilities

rules.description: Use ES6 classes for object-oriented code
rules.rationale: Classes provide cleaner syntax and better inheritance

rules.description: Use dependency injection for better testability
rules.rationale: Dependency injection improves testability and modularity

rules.description: Use EventEmitter for decoupled communication
rules.rationale: Event-driven architecture improves decoupling

rules.description: Use connection pooling for database connections
rules.rationale: Connection pooling improves performance and resource management

rules.description: Use transactions for multi-step operations
rules.rationale: Transactions ensure data consistency and integrity

rules.description: Implement graceful shutdown for database connections
rules.rationale: Graceful shutdown prevents data corruption and connection leaks

rules.description: Add rate limiting to API endpoints
rules.rationale: Rate limiting prevents abuse and DoS attacks

rules.description: Add authentication to protected endpoints
rules.rationale: Authentication protects sensitive operations

rules.description: Use consistent response structure
rules.rationale: Consistent responses improve API usability

rules.description: Add centralized error handling middleware
rules.rationale: Centralized error handling ensures consistent error responses

rules.description: Use structured logging with proper log levels
rules.replacement: Logger with levels (debug, info, warn, error)
rules.rationale: Structured logging improves debugging and monitoring

rules.description: Include context in log messages
rules.replacement: Logs with request ID, user ID, etc.
rules.rationale: Context helps trace issues across distributed systems

rules.description: Add unit tests for business logic
rules.rationale: Unit tests ensure code correctness and prevent regressions

rules.description: Add integration tests for API endpoints
rules.rationale: Integration tests verify end-to-end functionality

ibm_standards.error_handling: Centralized error handling with custom error classes
ibm_standards.logging: Winston or Bunyan with structured logging
